newsitem.title: USA: IMP to cut staff, sees significant losses.
newsitem.headline: IMP to cut staff, sees significant losses.

text.p: IMP Inc., a maker of mixed integrated circuits, said Monday it expected to report a "significant" second-quarter loss due to weaker demand for computer chips and restructuring charges.
In a statement, the company said it has cut 89 jobs and was also planning periodic factory shut downs to match production with demand.
A spokesman for the San Jose, Calif.-based company said the reductions were in addition to the 51 job cuts announced in August.
In the second quarter of fiscal 1996, IMP reported a profit of $1.1 million, or 4 cents a share, on revenues of $18.5 million.
IMP's stock rose 50 cents to $6.50 on Nasdaq.
